scope: Step-plan stage (01-step-plan.md) and page intro (00-intro.md): claude-sonnet-5-5 inline run of node-fix-bug on ShipLoop 1.3.0 / plugin 2.3.1 (seeded at step-plan, one context). Proposals checked against the generators at main da9e2e75 (ShipLoop 1.5.0) and branch shiploop-eff-loop-6afcbc (0d462ca4); step-plan rendered offline at main with 70- and 164-character run dirs (scratchpad/eff2/render-stepplan).

findings.where: shiploop_loops.HOST_LINE and INVOKE_LINE (branch -loop- 0d462ca4; at main the 'How to invoke:' line in invoke_lines); test/shiploop-loops.test.py test_the_host_line_names_the_skill_tool_and_the_command_for_every_other_host; skills/shiploop/SKILL.md 'Stage Until Loops'
findings.observation: Step-plan took 9 tool calls in 36 s. Call 4 was Skill {skill: "until-loop", args: Work+Contract+Receipt} and returned '<tool_use_error>Unknown skill: until-loop</tool_use_error>'; the model said 'The skill isn't registered; the packet points to the ADAPTER card', spent call 5 on grep ADAPTER.md (2,550 chars) to learn 'python3 <script> start --receipt <Receipt> < <Contract>', then wrote the result first ('Write the result first, then start the loop') and ran one 'trivial' iteration, against 'Do this stage's work only inside that loop'. skill-craft registers no until-loop skill (the runtime is vendored at skills/improve/runtime/until-loop; the published plugin is listed as until-loop:until-loop), so the bare name cannot resolve. The 1.3.0 packet printed no start command; branch -loop- prints it but HOST_LINE still sends Claude first to 'the Skill tool, skill "until-loop"'. Later stages skipped the Skill call from memory; a cleared stage (S-6) would repeat the failure in each of the 7 looped stages.
findings.proposal: One start line for every host; drop the Skill-tool fork. INVOKE_LINE = 'RUN the Until Loop now, once; the lines between the two markers are its contract (the Contract file already holds them). Do this stage's work only inside the loop.' HOST_LINE = 'Start it with this command, in the foreground, on every host; then follow each packet it prints (run its done_argv as printed) until the receipt says complete or stopped:' (start_command line unchanged). Replace the HOST_LINE test with one asserting 'Skill tool' is absent and start_command is the next line; reword SKILL.md ('on Claude Code the Skill tool until-loop'). Exit check: grep -rn 'skill "until-loop"\|skill until-loop' skills/shiploop finds none, and a Claude slice has no Skill call named until-loop.
findings.generic_ok: yes: no platform word; the Bash start command is identical on every host and hook-visible.
findings.risk: Owner asked for 'RUN the skill' wording: keep the verb, drop the tool name. A host that registers an until-loop skill loses nothing (the command is what its card runs). Pins to update: the HOST_LINE text test, at main the 'Skill tool with skill until-loop' assertion in test/shiploop-loops.test.py, and SKILL.md.
findings.plan_ref: 3.6 / D-3: exit 'a Claude E2E on the two-line argument passes' assumes the Skill route works on Claude; this run shows it does not
findings.est_effect: 2 of 9 calls and about 2.6k of ~69.6k ingested characters in a cold step-plan; up to 14 calls per item when every stage is cold; restores the start-then-work order.

findings.where: shiploop_navigator._first_callback_lines (Callback line); shiploop_prompts.STAGE_RULES and PROGRESS_RULE; shiploop_status_hook._verb
findings.observation: All 15 ShipLoop `complete` calls I could parse in the run (check-only and real) were piped ('2>&1 | head -50') and/or built from shell variables ('R=...', '$SC complete ... --result=$R/inbox/$A.md'). I ran shiploop_status_hook._verb on those shapes: None for each (a bare 'R=' prefix alone is accepted), so the status hook never fired: 'PostToolUse:Bash says' appears once in 14 stage files, after the first unpiped `next`. 'Show the user this narrative exactly as written' was echoed in 0 of 9 recorded model messages, so the owner saw ShipLoop's status once. The rule meant to prevent this is one clause with no reason, ignored 15 of 15: 'Run ShipLoop commands in the foreground, unpiped'.
findings.proposal: Put the reason on the line the model copies. Callback line: 'Callback for this stage (run once after its work, with the result written to the file it names; run it exactly as printed, with no pipe, redirect, `;` or shell variable: the status display and keepalive read the command and its whole output): <cmd>'. STAGE_RULES bullet: '- Run each ShipLoop command in the foreground exactly as printed (no pipe, redirect, `;` or variable), and never end the turn while one runs.' PROGRESS_RULE gains 'exactly as printed'. Test through the real hook: the printed callback, its --check-only form, next and pause return a verb; a planted pipe returns None. Live check: every `complete` command in a slice matches _verb.
findings.generic_ok: yes: host-neutral; names the hook's contract, no platform.
findings.risk: Habit may survive wording, so the live count is the test. The hook cannot tolerate pipes without losing the whole-output guarantee (head -N cuts it). About +200 chars on the head; offset by 3.2's dropped --result flag (about -190 chars at a 164-char dir).
findings.plan_ref: 3.2(d) (RULES bullet) and principle 5 (hooks must see every command); this adds the measured rate and the reason
findings.est_effect: hook coverage of `complete` 0 of 15 to a target of 15 of 15; keepalive and status rebind every stage; net bytes about zero.

findings.where: shiploop_navigator.emit and packet_head (the footer sentence 'The duties and rules above are this stage's; the full packet adds ...'); render (section order of the file)
findings.observation: The 1.3.0 head (12,417 chars, from `next`) said 'Read the full packet before acting'; the model read the whole file (29,175 chars) and 11,344 of the head's chars (91%) reappear verbatim in it (41.6k ingested for a 28.3k packet). At main the head leads with the duties, yet 15,716 of its 19,395 chars (81%, 70-char dir) are still in the file, and the footer still says 'Read it with a file-reading tool'. The file adds only the original request, the knowledge files and hand-offs, guide links and the last-accepted block (about 8.1k at main), scattered through it. In this run the one Read happened in step-plan; the 7 later long-packet stages made 0 Reads and worked from heads of 3.4k-7.4k chars that omitted the duties. The printed head also omits the delegation prefix the file starts with (inline: 'Continue in this context ... never clear or hand it off'; ask-agent: 'Execute the prompt in a fresh context'), checked on both routes at main. Host fact in the plan: offsets on run-directory files are honoured 164 of 164.
findings.proposal: Replace the footer sentence with a script-filled one: 'The head above is complete for this stage's duties, rules, result shape and loop. The full packet repeats it and adds, at these lines of {path}: the original request {a}-{b}; the knowledge files and hand-offs {c}-{d}; guide links {e}-{f}. Open only a range you need, with a file-reading tool (offset and limit), not the shell; after a lost context read the file whole once.' emit() computes the ranges from the spans render() gives the blocks the head omits (build the head without the footer, then add it); the text is identical on every print (no warm or cold variant). Also print guidance.inner_context(route) as the head's first line (plan 5.5). Test: every file line absent from the head lies inside a printed range, and the numbers point at them.
findings.generic_ok: yes: derived from section spans, no domain words.
findings.risk: Mechanical but must track render() order: record spans while rendering rather than searching for markers. S-6 holds: the file stays complete and the footer says to read it whole after a lost context. About +0 bytes (the new sentence is about as long as the old one).
findings.plan_ref: 1.2 / D-27 assume the file repeats the head and accept a cut tail; 3.3 / 5.5 already put the delegation line first; the range footer is not in the plan
findings.est_effect: per long packet that is read after its head: -11k chars (1.3.0 step-plan, of 41.6k) to -15.7k (main step-plan, of 43.5k); node-fix-bug at main has five heads over 14k (79.9k printed).

findings.where: vendored skills/improve/runtime/until-loop/scripts/until_loop_ephemeral.py (start and done returns); shiploop_loops._PACKET_KEYS and check_loop_packet
findings.observation: One loop iteration ingested 20,082 chars of runtime JSON: the unfiltered `start` return is 13,098 chars (instruction 5,803; context 2,623; work+conditions 1,671, which repeat the packet's Argument block; report_schema 1,131) and the terminal `done` return is 6,984, of which about 5,218 repeat the start return (context, conditions, work, status_semantics, receipt, workspace, state_file, progress). In each of the 6 later loops the model piped the runtime through python3 -c printing only state_file, done_argv[-1] and (twice) conditions.exit: it keeps what it needs and drops the rest, but only after paying once, and a cleared stage pays again.
findings.proposal: Extend 6.5's lean print to the `start` return and the terminal `done` return: status, state_file, done_argv, next_argv, a two-sentence instruction and the report_schema field names; work, conditions and context stay in the contract and the receipt (check_loop_packet keeps comparing the receipt's full key set). Do not suggest piping the start return in the packet: its instruction is authoritative for the first iteration.
findings.risk: Vendored runtime change: D-5 owner go, upstream release and re-vendor; the main-tenet probe of D-19 applies.
findings.plan_ref: 6.5 / D-19 (covers a non-terminal done only); D-5
findings.est_effect: 20,082 to about 4k chars for the first loop in a context (about -16k), again per cold stage; warm stages already filter it themselves.

findings.where: shiploop_loops.WORK, the step-plan and test-spec entries ('... then run the `complete --check-only` command printed there and fix each refusal')
findings.observation: No packet prints a `complete --check-only` command; the packet prints only the Callback. The model derived the command by inserting the flag, correctly 15 of 15 (step-plan accepted at the first check-only: 'every script gate for step-plan accepts this result'). The sentence 'printed there' is false. The loop's `exit_checks` is [] and `last_check_results` null, so 'satisfied' in the done report ('All 7 exit conditions hold') is the model's own claim.
findings.proposal: Zero-byte wording fix in the two loops.WORK entries: '... then run the Callback command with --check-only added and fix each refusal.' Add a printed line only if a live run shows a model failing to derive it. Considered and deferred (KISS): freeze the check-only command as the contract's exit_checks (runtime 0.8.3 then refuses a satisfied report without a fresh recorded run); no failure was observed and verify_script is a multi-line heredoc the model must paste unchanged.
findings.risk: Changes the contract text of two stages (rebuilt from state, so a run in flight keeps its own); no test quotes the phrase.
findings.plan_ref: 8.1 (false sentences, '_checked_line' prints every refusal first); principle 11 (exits are script-run) for the deferred exit_checks option
findings.est_effect: about 0 bytes; removes one false pointer; exit_checks option unmeasured.

findings.observation: The 3 ShipLoop refusals of the run were all in test-spec, not step-plan (step-plan: 0 refusals, 0 reads of ShipLoop source). Refusal 1: 'test_cases[0] needs exactly id, criterion, requirement, oracle, red, green'; refusal 2: the same text after a BSD `sed -i` failed and changed nothing; refusal 3: 'TC-1 names R-3' with no entry in HOME/spec.md. The seed records spec, discovery and test-strategy without writing HOME/spec.md, environment.md or architecture.md ('HOME/spec.md: not written yet (spec writes it)'), so the model wrote a spec itself. The refusal's hard-coded example '"requirement": "R-3"' (the template says R-1) was copied: 'Requirement is expected as R-3; I'll use it.' The same gap left step-plan's duties on R-n, follows, ## Commands and architecture decisions unexercised, and 'ShipLoop refuses release-plan if ... HOME/environment.md' is a latent refusal 11 stages on. The Grok live run had zero refusals.
findings.proposal: (a) After advancing, write WORKTREE/docs/shiploop/spec.md with one neutral requirement 'R-1: <outcome from the case prompt>' and environment.md with '## Commands' holding the case's checks, so step cases run the normal path; keep a flagged no-HOME seed for the missing-file route. (b) In _TEST_CASE_SHAPE print '"requirement": "R-<n>"', not a literal id. No new step-plan gate: with a spec the quoted R-ids are in the packet and the Grok run needed none.
findings.risk: A richer seed hides the missing-file route; keep both variants. (b) touches a refusal text that tests quote.
findings.plan_ref: none (plan 1.1 fixtures cover offline renders, not the seed's HOME files)
findings.est_effect: removes 3 of 3 refusals in this slice and makes step-plan's R-n, follows and Knowledge duties testable.

findings.where: shiploop_prompts.py step-plan duty 9 ('Plan record'); new references/plan-record.md (at most 8 KB)
findings.observation: Duty items total 8,108 chars; item 9 is 2,287 (28%), its last four bullets (namespace and schema, pinned values, interactions/UI/service) are conditional, and it ends 'This record is supporting reference; each step's task and criteria stay its only directive'. The model skipped all nine bullets for a one-line fix (summary: 2 sentences) and the check-only gates did not notice. Items 1 and 2 (455 and 630 chars) were acted on in one clause.
findings.proposal: '9. **Plan record** (supporting reference; each step's task and criteria stay its only directive), in the item's `context` or the summary, for the topics this item touches only: outcome and invariants kept; contracts and responsibilities that change; target files, interfaces and conventions matched to the house style (House-style guidance); each step's failure cases and diagnostics; documentation to change; integration impact and release prerequisites. Also, when the item adds or moves code or stored data, replays pinned values, or changes interactions, UI or service state: record them as <GUIDES>/plan-record.md says.' Move the four conditional bullets verbatim into plan-record.md (one section each, the UI default of rich interaction intact), with a ledger row each.
findings.generic_ok: yes: topic triggers, no domain words; the file keeps the platform-neutral wording.
findings.risk: A model planning a UI change might not open the file: keep the trigger words 'interactions, UI or service state' in the duty and run the existing UI case in the battery; G-LEDGER for the moved obligations.

findings.where: shiploop_navigator.packet_head and render (section order); shiploop_prompts.STAGE_RULES; plan steps 1.0(b), 1.2, 3.1
findings.observation: Packet of 28,303 chars at a 190-char path root: duties 8,108 (29%); guide and queue lines 3,581 (13%, 0 of the 12 guide links opened); loop block 2,943; Checked-by 1,319; template 1,681; literal paths about 6,301 (22%: RUN x20 = 2,840, skills x20 = 3,020, worktree x3 = 441). Script-provable same-packet duplicates: about 370 chars (the work-item sentence twice, the request's first clause in the narrative title) = 1.3%, so dedupe yields nothing here; the rest are paraphrases (Checked-by vs Exit list vs duties), which no script proves. In that file the duties start at char 18,514 (65%): a 20,000-char cut keeps items 1-2 and drops 3-12, Optional, RULES, Pause and Halt (8,303 chars), and the loop contract's Work line names the file as the home of the duties. At main with a 164-char dir the head is 20,595 and the cut falls inside 'How to invoke:' (the loop block is the last 3.1k of the head; Full packet, Progress view, footer, Recovery and Pause sit before it, 15,995-17,474); the merged tree adds about 1,350 and pushes the later part of the block (Contract, Receipt, the start command) toward or past the cut.
findings.proposal: Head order for inner producers: header with the delegation line; Callback; Goal; Done-when; Checked-by; Keepalive marker; status; narrative; Until Loop block; Current stage guidance with RULES; References; Result template and outcomes; then Full packet, Progress view, footer, Recovery, Pause (cut first). The status block stays before char 16,000 (hook WINDOW). Make the file follow the same order for those blocks so a truncated file read also keeps the duties. Cut nothing else: step-plan size comes from conditional text (SP-8), literal paths (3.1) and order, not duplicates.
findings.risk: About 230 text pins and the order-sensitive suites (packet-recut, completeness) change together; reorder first, reword later.
findings.plan_ref: 1.0(b), 1.2 (P0 order and cut test), D-27, 3.1; adds the file-order point and measured positions
findings.est_effect: no bytes; keeps the loop start, the duties and RULES inside the first ~18k on every host cut.

works_well: First-try acceptance with no ShipLoop-source reads: 'ShipLoop check-only: every script gate for step-plan accepts this result' and the real complete accepted the same file; 0 reads of shiploop_*.py, SKILL.md or any reference in 9 calls (the Grok live run read ShipLoop's text in 120 of 387 turns). Keep the numbered Exit list, the template with the receipt prefilled in evidence_refs, and the printed vocabulary (suite focused|regression|check; state works|broken|absent).
Duty 4's sizing rule ('A single bug fix or mechanical rename is one step') and duty 3's 'Confirm by: ...; pass when ...' shape were followed verbatim: one step, two criteria in the required form.
'Change no product file in this stage' was obeyed: the only write was the inbox result (plus the loop receipt).
The done report cited all seven numbered exit conditions, so the Exit list works as the model's checklist and the contract's wording is usable as evidence.

The printed absolute paths (callback, result, receipt) were reused without a single path error across the 15 `complete` calls; keep them literal (principle 5) and fix the pipe and variable habit with reasons (SP-2), not with symbols.
The head 'Full packet:' line plus the file gave a model with no ShipLoop memory every duty, rule and the template: the 1.3.0 packet was sufficient to plan correctly in one pass (36 s).
not_measured: Behaviour of the 1.5.0 head (duties first, 19,395 chars at a 70-char dir, 20,595 at 164) on a live model: the artifact is 1.3.0, whose head omits the duties; whether a model still reads the whole file after the new head is unmeasured (SP-3 sizes are offline).
A cleared or compacted context: the run is one inline context, so what a cold model does at each stage (repeat the Skill call, re-read the file, re-learn the runtime JSON) is inferred.
Real HOME files: the seed wrote none, so duties on R-n, follows, ## Commands and architecture decisions were unexercised; the late release-plan refusal never ran.
Multi-step plans, the ask-agent route, Grok, Codex and any platform case: one bug-fix item with one step on Claude.
